title: Order-flow imbalance / world order flow predicts crypto returns
economic_hypothesis: Net aggressive order flow is the direct footprint of liquidity demand. Aggregated order flow should therefore explain contemporaneous returns and carry out-of-sample predictive power beyond standard predictors.
entry_rules: UNKNOWN (regression-based predictive evidence; no rule set at the level read)
claimed_metrics: order flow has strong explanatory and predictive power for cryptocurrency returns out of sample, over and above standard economic predictors
required_data: exchange order flow (Binance klines carry taker-buy volume, which is a usable aggregate proxy; aggTrades give the tick version)
external_results: Conference paper (EFMA 2025) with out-of-sample predictive results.
counter_evidence: The project has ALREADY tested this family on its own data and closed it: A-01 flow imbalance (gross +0.481 bps), A-02 large-clip imbalance (+0.031), A-03 flow + breakout (+0.614), A-06 BTC lead/lag (+0.553), all COST_KILLED against a 23.791 bps round trip (docs/AGGTRADES_RESULTS_V1.md).
The reentry policy forbids re-entering a closed family under renamed rules; a more elaborate aggregation of the same flow is not a new opportunity.
The claimed edge is a statistical predictive relation; nothing in the source shows a net-of-cost executable line.
ambiguities: The source's 'world order flow' aggregation is not defined at the level read and is not obviously reconstructible.
No magnitude in bps per trade is available.
replication_difficulty: LOW technically, but it is a closed line.
evidence_quality: MEDIUM-HIGH as statistical evidence, NEGATIVE as an opportunity because the internal, better-controlled test already measured the cost kill.
selection_note: Registered explicitly so that a future reader cannot mistake the external paper for an untested opportunity: the same family was tested internally with the project's own cost model and died at the cost floor.
